table.tieBreaker1: Season-end tie-breaker 1: teams with more completed races are placed higher when points are tied.
table.tieBreaker2: Season-end tie-breaker 2: if points and completed races are tied, team race reputation decides.
table.tieBreakers: Tie-breakers: points → races completed → race reputation → A-Z.

rules.title: Season-end rules, playoffs and tie-breakers
rules.subtitle: Final ranking, promotion, playoff and relegation rules.
rules.intro: These rules are used when the season closes and the game decides final ranking, promotion places, playoff places and relegation places.
rules.ranking2: If points are equal: completed races, highest first.
rules.ranking3: If still equal: team race reputation, highest first.
rules.ranking4: If still equal: team name alphabetically A-Z.
rules.zeroPoints: This also solves zero-point teams: teams with more completed races stay above teams with fewer completed races.
rules.directText: Green rows are automatic promotion places. These teams move up directly at the season transition if the backend season-end job confirms the same final order.
rules.playoffText: Blue rows are playoff places. These teams are not promoted directly. They enter a season-end playoff against other qualified teams, and the playoff result decides the remaining promotion places.
rules.relegationText: Red rows are relegation places. At the end of the season, teams in these positions move down to the lower tier or lower division according to the league structure.
rules.proGuide: ProTeam West/East: winner promoted directly, 2nd-4th enter World playoff, bottom 5 are relegated.
rules.continentalGuide: Continental divisions: winner promoted directly, 2nd-4th enter Pro playoff, relegation count depends on the division.
rules.amateurGuide: Amateur divisions: promotion and playoff places depend on the region. Oceania promotes the top 3 directly.

tutorial.welcomeBody: We can show you how team rankings, competition tiers, international points, promotion, and relegation work.
tutorial.competitionsBody:
This is the Team Ranking page.

Here you can see rankings for all competitions and tiers, including WorldTeam, ProTeam, Continental, and Amateur divisions.

Each team has a place in its competition based on international points earned during the season. You can switch between tiers and divisions to see how teams are ranked across the whole cycling world.
tutorial.pointsBody:
Teams earn international points from races. Better results in bigger races usually bring more points.

These points decide the ranking position of each team inside its competition. At the end of the season, teams can be promoted to a higher tier or relegated to a lower tier depending on their final position.

This page is important because it shows where your team stands compared with other teams, and what you need to achieve to move up.

After Team Ranking, the next recommended page is Statistics.
